chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Sa'id, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamun al-Basri, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Mis'mam ibn Abd al-Malik Kirdin Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) set the reward for the runaway slave at one dinar if he is captured in his city, and if he is captured outside his city, then four dinars."

The Book of Earnings has concluded, and it will be followed by the Book of Trade, if God wills. 'And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' * And prayer upon Muhammad and his pure family. Concluded by the grace and help of God what we intended regarding commentary and extraction of hadiths on the sixth part of the Book of Tahdhib al-Ahkam according to our division, and we ask God for assistance to complete the extraction of the remaining parts, and that was done by the poor one who confesses to disobedience, Hassan al-Mawssawi al-Khorasani, and all praise is to God alone.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on the reward for capturing a runaway slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific financial incentive (jaul) for capturing a runaway slave (abiq), distinguishing between one dinar for capture within the city of residence and four dinars for capture elsewhere. This differential reward structure reflects the practical realities of the time, accounting for the greater effort and risk involved in tracking a slave outside their known territory, a principle often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding lost property and rewards.
